typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source slide 8 / navBack.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source slide 8 / navBack.

recognitionRules: Use restrained Helvetica Neue with a large numerical scope marker.
Set the required result beside the client’s retained responsibility.
Use red sparingly to identify the choice under discussion.
Keep pricing assumptions and non-commitment language near the comparison.

principles: Name the choice, its owner and the condition that makes it complete.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: Start with the result you need. Then choose the support that fits.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid certainty about forecasts, capacity or commitments that are still provisional.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: This is the assumption; this is the decision it affects.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use VALUE IN VIEW as a Helvetica Neue wordmark above one short red rule. No trophy, checkmark or upward arrow.
invariants: Use restrained Helvetica Neue with a large numerical scope marker.
Set the required result beside the client’s retained responsibility.
Use red sparingly to identify the choice under discussion.
adaptations: A concise proposal can retain only brief, routes and decision.
Change the service while preserving the comparison logic.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.
